methods_compared: Scanpy standard vs Seurat v5 standard
metric_summary: Median nominal outputs were nearly identical under the same declared inputs: cells after QC 2699 vs 2698, median counts 2197.0 vs 2196.5, median genes 817 vs 816, and median cluster count 5 vs 5.
runtime_summary: This block targets nominal output comparability rather than pipeline wall-time.
interpretation: Standardized wrappers recover expected baseline behavior without claiming algorithmic superiority.

methods_compared: Baseline scanpy-standard vs Harmony vs scVI
metric_summary: Batch-mixing medians were 0.002 for the baseline embedding, 0.127 for Harmony, and 0.091 for scVI. Harmony remained close to the baseline clustering structure (ARI 0.808, 95% CI 0.804-0.817), while scVI remained close to Harmony (ARI 0.771, 95% CI 0.764-0.775).
runtime_summary: Successful-run median wall time was 21.0 s for Harmony and 42.8 s for scVI; success rates were 11/11 and 20/24, respectively.
interpretation: The framework captures method-level trade-offs between mixing, structural agreement, and operational cost under standardized inputs.

metric_summary: Pairwise spotwise cosine medians were 0.364 (IQR 0.234-0.495) for RCTD/Tangram, 0.633 (0.557-0.689) for Tangram/cell2location, and 0.494 (0.421-0.558) for RCTD/cell2location. Representative mean-entropy medians were 1.986, 2.411, and 3.091, respectively.
runtime_summary: Successful-run median wall time was 1853.2 s for RCTD, 290.9 s for Tangram, and 481.9 s for cell2location; success rates were 5/5, 5/5, and 4/11, respectively.
interpretation: Different spatial mapping models lead to materially different composition vectors and operational footprints, which motivates explicit audit outputs rather than a single-method claim.
